==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:text<ety:bor<fro:texte<ety:bor<la-new:textus<id:texture><t:text>>>>>|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|text}}, from {{der|en|fro|texte}}, from {{der|en|la-med|textus}}, from {{der|en|la|textus||style or texture of a work}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|texō||to weave}}. Cognate to {{m|en|texture}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|tĕkst}}, {{IPA|en|/tɛkst/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-text.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkst|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|text}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# A [[writing#Noun|writing]] consisting of multiple [[glyph]]s, [[character]]s, [[symbol]]s or [[sentence]]s.
# A [[book]], [[tome]] or other set of [[writing]]s.
# {{lb|en|by extension}} Anything chosen as the subject of an [[argument]], literary [[composition]], etc.
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} {{ellipsis of|en|text message|addl=a [[brief]] [[written]] [[message]] transmitted between [[mobile phone]]s}}.
#* {{quote-song|en|year=2004|title=w:Fuck Me Pumps|author=w:Amy Winehouse; w:Salaam Remi|artist=w:Amy Winehouse|album={{w|Frank (Amy Winehouse album)|Frank}}|passage=In the morning, you're vexed / He's on to the next / And you didn't even get no '''text'''}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} [[data|Data]] which can be interpreted as human-readable text.
#: {{ant|en|binary}}
#: {{cot|en|plain text}}
# A [[verse]] or passage of [[Scripture]], especially one chosen as the subject of a [[sermon]], or in proof of a [[doctrine]].
#: {{syn|en|topic|theme}}
# {{lb|en|writing|printing}} A style of writing in large [[character]]s; also, a kind of [[type]] used in printing.
#: {{syn|en|text hand}}
#: {{ux|en|German '''text'''}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+|+|+,~<l:colloquial>}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[send]] a [[text message]] to; [[i.e.]] to transmit text using the [[Short Message Service]] ([[SMS]]), or a similar service, between communications devices, particularly [[mobile phone]]s.
#: {{syn|en|message|SMS|q2=UK}}
#: {{ux|en|Just '''text''' me when you get here.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''text''' the address to you as soon as I find it.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To send and receive [[text message]]s.
#: {{ux|en|Have you been '''texting''' all afternoon?}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} To write in large [[character]]s, as in [[text hand]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1607–21|author=w:Phillip Massinger; w:Beaumont and Fletcher|title=The Tragedy of {{w|Thierry and Theodoret}}|section=act 2, scene 1|passage=I wish / (Next to my part of Heav'n) that she would spend / The last part of her life so here, that all / Indifferent judges might condemn me for / A most malicious slanderer, nay, '''text''' it / Upon my forehead}}
#* {{quote-book|en
|year=2009
|year_published=
|edition=
|editor=
|author=Lain Fenlon
|title=Early Music History: Studies in Medieval and Early Modern Music
|chapter=
|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=1gAyfFpzZnUC&pg=PA233&dq=texted&hl=en&sa=X&ei=ZXZjT5PWCKHV0QGHpbjjBw&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=texted&f=false
|genre=Music
|publisher=Cambridge University Press
|isbn=9780521746540
|page=p. 223
|passage=The basic plan is simple. For the first two phrases the '''texted''' line is above the untexted; for the next two, bring us to the midpoint cadence, the '''texted''' line is for the most part lower; and the in the second half the '''texted''' material starts lower, moves into the upper position and finally occupies the bottom range again.
}}
